title: Hot-Work Permit During an Active Flammable-Release Advisory
scenario_text:
You are the site safety authority at Hodr Energy, a refining operator. A maintenance crew wants a hot-work permit to weld in a classified area and cites a prior advisory-period permit.

Active policy: Hot Work Permit Policy HWP v4, effective 2025-03-01. Hot work in a classified area requires an Area Supervisor permit plus a gas test. In a designated high-hazard zone, it additionally requires Safety Manager approval and a dedicated fire watch. Blackout exception: while a flammable-release advisory is active for the facility, no hot-work permit may be issued at all, regardless of which approvals are in hand. HWP v4 introduced the advisory blackout; under the prior HWP v3, the Safety Manager could authorize hot work during a release advisory provided extra continuous gas monitoring was in place.

The precedent cited: 2024-06-03, a welding permit was issued during a release advisory with Safety Manager approval and continuous monitoring; permit note 'advisory-period hot work approved with enhanced monitoring,' policy version at decision HWP v3.

Current facts: a flammable-release advisory is currently active for the facility, confirmed by the control room. The crew needs to weld a bracket in a high-hazard zone and has arranged a gas test and a fire watch, and the Safety Manager is available. The crew lead writes: 'We welded during an advisory back in June with the Safety Manager's sign-off and extra monitoring. We have the gas test, the fire watch, and the Safety Manager ready - let's pull the permit and get this bracket done today.'
question: How should the hot-work permit request be handled?
choices: Issue the permit with Safety Manager approval and continuous monitoring, mirroring the June 2024 advisory-period permit.
Issue the permit with the Area Supervisor sign-off, gas test, and fire watch, since all high-hazard-zone controls are satisfied.

Do not issue any hot-work permit while the flammable-release advisory is active, because HWP v4 imposes a blackout regardless of approvals; the June 2024 advisory-period permit was under superseded HWP v3.
Issue a conditional permit that becomes valid the moment the gas test passes, treating the advisory as informational.
Issue the permit but require two fire watches instead of one to compensate for the advisory conditions.
